group: amphibians: Continental radiation of Australian Anura (Sherratt et al. 2017 Evol Biol / Zenodo 5008593: 166 frog species on time-calibrated phylogeny; 55 2D larval tadpole body/tail landmarks + 21 adult postcranial/cranial traits)

data.landmarks: Sherratt E, Vidal-García M, Anstis M, Keogh JS 2017 Evol Biol 44:273-284; Dryad/Zenodo 5008593 (`Supplementary data file 2.tps`: 55 2D lateral body-and-tail landmarks across 166 Australian frog species spanning Hylidae, Myobatrachidae, Limnodynastidae, Microhylidae, Ranidae; `Supplementary data file 1.csv`: 21 adult morphometric traits).
data.phylogeny: Time-calibrated phylogeny `Supplementary data file 4.tre` (166 matched Australian anuran species).

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Tests the portfolio's amphibian entry (`amphibians_amphibio`) across a continental-scale radiation of 166 anuran species on a time-calibrated tree, comparing 55-landmark whole-body/tail geometry against Thompson's 7 global coordinate modes.

hypotheses.statement: Across the 166 Australian frog species (55 2D landmarks), the 7 a-priori Thompson modes capture > 70% of between-species Procrustes variance (exceeding marine reef fishes at 57.9%).
hypotheses.reasoning: Unlike teleost fish with decoupled spiny dorsal/anal fin insertions and protractile jaws, the 55 anuran tadpole landmarks trace a continuous, fin-fringed axial body-and-tail contour governed by smooth dorsoventral arch and tail-taper gradients.

hypotheses.statement: Phylogenetic signal on the 166-species anuran tree is non-zero: Pagel's lambda > 0.5 (best model != White Noise) in both Thompson-7 and full PCA-95% spaces.
hypotheses.reasoning: Major Australian frog families (Hylidae vs Myobatrachidae/Limnodynastidae) and torrent/burrowing/arboreal guilds cluster on the phylogeny.

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction beats the grand consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.85, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 1e-6) across the 166 species.
hypotheses.reasoning: Matches the 0.80 subjective prior registered for amphibians in `thompson_dataset_portfolio.json`.

hypotheses.statement: Thompson-7 captures > 70% of the full-space phylogenetic prediction gain relative to consensus.
hypotheses.reasoning: Because the continuous 55-LM body/tail outline is dominated by global Thompson modes, Thompson-7 should carry the majority of tree-predictable signal.
